migration.migration_reason: Preserved paid Ecosystem findings/citations were centrally re-adjudicated under the current runner-owned fixed rubric. Legacy language-local scores were not copied.

metric.external_integration_coverage.candidate_universe: For each sub-dimension the specific library/target was chosen by a declared external, benchmark-independent criterion: the vendor's own officially designated SDK repository (aws/aws-sdk-go-v2, Azure/azure-sdk-for-go, googleapis/google-cloud-go), the CNCF/Kubernetes project's own reference client (kubernetes/client-go), and the gRPC project's own reference implementation repository (grpc/grpc-go), each retrieved via one route (official project README/package documentation).

component_findings.c_native: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Go has a mature messaging ecosystem (official NATS Go client, Confluent's official Kafka Go client, widely used RabbitMQ/AMQP libraries) plus a strong standard-library HTTP stack and popular third-party web frameworks, though some of these (e.g. Kafka, RabbitMQ clients) are community/vendor-maintained rather than uniformly first-party across every messaging system.
component_findings.database_data: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Go has a broad, mature database ecosystem: the standard library's database/sql interface plus mature drivers (pgx, go-sql-driver/mysql) for relational databases, an official MongoDB driver, and an official go-redis client for Redis.
component_findings.extension_embedding: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Sub-scores rely on a small set of declared representative libraries per domain rather than an exhaustive audit of every possible integration; library selection used official project self-designation (official SDK/reference-implementation repos) as the external, benchmark-independent selection rule.
component_findings.language_bindings: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): grpc-go is the Go reference implementation of gRPC maintained by the gRPC project itself, alongside official protobuf-go bindings, giving Go first-party, reference-quality RPC/serialization support.
component_findings.network_cloud: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): AWS, Azure and GCP each publish and actively maintain official first-party Go SDKs. AWS SDK for Go v2 reached general availability and is described as the official AWS SDK for Go; Google Cloud publishes official Go Cloud Client Libraries; Azure publishes monthly Go SDK releases.

metric.external_integration_coverage.limitations: Sub-scores rely on a small set of declared representative libraries per domain rather than an exhaustive audit of every possible integration; library selection used official project self-designation (official SDK/reference-implementation repos) as the external, benchmark-independent selection rule.
metric.external_integration_coverage.selection_rule: Evaluate working documented integrations and binding ecosystems, not only theoretical FFI design; FFI language design itself belongs to Language Quality.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.candidate_universe: Source of truth is the Go project's own 'go tool dist list' output and go.dev/doc/install/source GOOS enumeration, cross-checked against secondary reproductions of the same command output. Same retrieval route (official Go docs + reproduced 'go tool dist list' output) used as would be used for any other language's official target-list documentation.

component_findings.architectures: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Frozen rubric applied identically to all 10 languages: score = sum of 5 sub-dimensions x 20 pts, based on breadth of platforms actually supported/shippable by the official toolchain/runtime as of the snapshot date (2026-09-22). Sub-dimensions: (1) tier-1 desktop OS coverage (Windows/macOS/Linux) with first-class official support; (2) breadth of CPU architectures officially supported for native code generation (x86-32/64, ARM 32/64, RISC-V, PPC64, s390x, MIPS, WASM, etc.); (3) mobile OS targets (iOS/Android) reachable via the official toolchain, including whether it is a first-class core capability or requires a secondary/experimental subrepo; (4) Web/WASM target support built into the standa
component_findings.desktop_server_os: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Windows, macOS (darwin) and Linux are all tier-1, first-class, officially supported host and target platforms; Go's own docs demonstrate straightforward cross-compilation to all three from a single machine.
component_findings.embedded: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Proxy relies on the vendor-published target-list command/documentation rather than independent verification that every listed target is production-grade; 'go tool dist list' includes some 'known-broken' ports per Go's own porting policy, which the rubric partially penalizes in the other_embedded_legacy_os sub-score.
component_findings.mobile: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): android and ios are directly listed as first-party GOOS values in the official install-from-source documentation and in 'go tool dist list' (android/arm64, ios/arm64, etc.), so cross-compiling Go code for phone OSes is a built-in toolchain capability. However, turnkey mobile *application* packaging/UI still depends on the separate golang.org/x/mobile (gomobile) subrepo rather than being a fully first-class, batteries-included app-build pipeline the way it is for some mobile-native languages, so this sub-dimension is scored below the maximum.
component_findings.web_wasm_other: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-5--go): Go ships official js/wasm and wasip1/wasm GOOS/GOARCH targets directly in the standard toolchain enumeration, giving first-party browser and WASI target support without third-party compilers.

metric.implemented_platform_coverage.limitations: Proxy relies on the vendor-published target-list command/documentation rather than independent verification that every listed target is production-grade; 'go tool dist list' includes some 'known-broken' ports per Go's own porting policy, which the rubric partially penalizes in the other_embedded_legacy_os sub-score.
metric.implemented_platform_coverage.selection_rule: Count only platforms with currently implemented and documented build/run support; design intent without working support does not count.

snapshot_recertification.policy: legacy evidence re-adjudicated under current runner-owned rubric
